title: S&P Select Sector Indices December rebalance — the Quarterly Qualification Date close (sets the capped weights the 12-18 effective trade must print)
source: EST: date derived by applying an SEC-filed rule to the 2026 calendar. SEC EDGAR, Select Sector SPDR Trust Form 497 (accession 0001193125-26-031948, document d85739d497.htm), fetched direct 2026-09-08 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 2,388,335 bytes — byte-identical to the 2026-09-04, 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-08 sibling fetches, a small integrity check that four independent sessions read the same document). This session extracted a DEFINED TERM no sibling ledger had quoted, which names the date directly rather than inferring it from the rebalancing sentence: 'If on the second Friday of any calendar quarter-end month (a "Quarterly Qualification Date"), a Component Stock (or two or more Component Stocks) approaches the maximum allowable value limits set forth above (the "Asset Diversification Limits"), the percentage that such Component Stock (or Component Stocks) represents in the Select Sector Index will be reduced...' The timing sentence corroborates: 'The rebalancing of the Select Sector Indices, based on the processes described above, occurs at the closing prices of the second Friday of March, June, September and December. Changes will become effective after the market close on the third Friday of March, June, September and December.' December 2026's Fridays are 12-04 / 12-11 / 12-18 / 12-25 (weekday arithmetic computed mechanically this session), so the Quarterly Qualification Date is Fri 2026-12-11 and the capping goes effective after the Fri 2026-12-18 close — which is opex-2026-12-18, confirmed independently on the OCC calendar. EDGAR submissions for CIK 0001064641 re-checked 2026-09-08 for supersession: the only filings after the 2026-06-12 redemption-procedure 497 are an N-CSRS (2026-09-03, semi-annual report, no rebalancing language) and routine NPORT-Ps, so the January 497 remains operative. Filed estimate rather than SEC:/confirmed on the same two counts every sibling in this sequence recorded: the filing dates the RULE, not this instance — S&P DJI's own methodology and Policies & Practices PDFs returned HTTP 403 again on 2026-09-08 and sectorspdrs.com serves no fetchable schedule — and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. The DATE is not in doubt; the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-08), which read the single proposal carrying this id (proposals/sp-rebalance-reference-close-2026-12-11.from-sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-12-31.json) in full first, then re-fetched the SEC primary and re-derived every number rather than inheriting the proposer's. Ledger: docs/research/events/sp-rebalance-reference-close-2026-12-11.md. BOTH QUESTIONS THE PROPOSAL LEFT OPEN ARE ANSWERED. (1) December has NO pro-forma release date distinct from this close: S&P DJI publishes capped / alternatively weighted pro-formas after the close of the second Friday, the same session as the Quarterly Qualification Date, so this one entry covers what September needed two for — and the calendar correctly carries no separate December capped-pro-forma entry. The December ADD/DROP file is the separate one, a week earlier, already proposed as sp-rebalance-proforma-2026-12-04. (2) The russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 collision is REAL AND UNPRECEDENTED but MEASURED TO BE IMMATERIAL to cap arithmetic. FTSE Russell's first-ever December semi-annual reconstitution is effective after the US close on the SECOND FRIDAY of December — the same session as this Quarterly Qualification Date — so for the first time in either family's history one closing auction both prints a Russell reconstitution trade and strikes the prices that set S&P Select Sector caps. Across 12 June reconstitution closes (2015-2026), top-name-versus-sector one-day excess-return dispersion on reconstitution day runs BELOW its all-day norm in 5 of 7 mega-cap pairs (AMZN/XLY 0.76x, XOM/XLE 0.48x, NVDA/XLK 0.69x, TSLA/XLY 0.46x, CVX/XLE 0.44x; only META/XLC 1.20x and GOOGL/XLC 1.05x exceed 1, n=9), and even IWM/SPY runs 0.77x. Reconstitution flow is a boundary and small-cap phenomenon; the cap tests bind on mega-caps. Execution color, not cap arithmetic. THE DECEMBER-SPECIFIC FINDING: the single-name cap most likely does NOT bind here. AMZN is the only name over 24% anywhere in the family today (24.65%, State Street issuer file self-dated 04-Sep-2026), gets cut to 23.00% after the 2026-09-18 close, and must then gain +4.35% versus XLY over the 59 sessions to this close to re-breach — which the exact September-third-Friday to December-second-Friday window delivered in only 2 of 11 years (2015, 2017), was NEGATIVE in 8 of 11, median -3.11%, against a 45.1% unconditional base rate. Whether a COHORT cap binds is not an open question but a QUEUED one: it is decided entirely by the filing-literal-versus-iterative fork registered as FT-sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12-1, which scores 2026-09-25, 77 days before this event needs it. Also unpriced by every prior sibling: the filing's STEP 4 ('if a Component Stock represents between 4.5% and 4.8% ... prior to the first three steps, the weight of such Component Stock shall be reduced to 4.5%') adds ~$131M to XLC and ~$70M to XLE, taking XLC's September capping trade from $73M to ~$204M. Low impact and market-structure only: it strikes prices, never prints a trade, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4/G1) is index-flow-keyed — re-grepped 2026-09-08, zero hits. Kind sector matches every sibling in the sequence.
